questions: When multiple people have the same score x, should they all receive the same rank r, and then r increments by k (the count of people with score x)?
If there are multiple distinct scores among undetermined people, which score x should be chosen in each iteration? The highest, lowest, or arbitrary?
Should the output be in the order of person labels (1 to N), or in the order of processing (e.g., grouped by score)?
If all scores are distinct, does the procedure still work (k=1 each time)?
Is r incremented before or after assigning ranks to the next group?
What if two groups have the same score but are processed in different iterations? Impossible because all with score x are processed together.
Should ties in score always be broken by assigning the same rank, or is there any tie‑breaking based on person label?
Is the initial value of r guaranteed to be 1, or could it be 0?
